record.paper_title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
record.original_question: For the Straubing-Thérien concatenation hierarchy of star-free languages over a finite alphabet A, level 0 consists of ∅ and A*, level n+1/2 consists of finite unions of marked products of languages from level n, and level n+1 consists of Boolean combinations of languages of marked products of level n. Given a half-integer n and a star-free language L, is there a decision procedure that determines whether L belongs to level n of this hierarchy?

evidence.quote:
The level 0
consists of the languages ∅ and A∗. The other levels are defined inductively
as follows:
(1) the level n+ 1/2 is the class of union of marked products of languages
of level n;
(2) the level n + 1 is the class of Boolean combination of languages of
marked products of level n.

Problem 2. Given a half integer n and a star-free language L, decide
whether L belongs to level n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ denote the free monoid of words over $A$. A language $L \subseteq A^*$ is called star-free if it can be obtained from the finite languages by finitely many applications of Boolean operations (union, intersection, complement) and concatenation, but without the use of the Kleene star.

A marked product of languages $L_0, L_1, \dots, L_k \subseteq A^*$ is a language of the form $L_0 a_1 L_1 a_2 L_2 \cdots a_k L_k$ where $a_1, \dots, a_k \in A$.

The Straubing-Thérien concatenation hierarchy is the family of classes of languages $\{\mathcal{V}_n\}$, indexed by half-integers $n \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{N}$, defined inductively by:
- Level $0$: $\mathcal{V}_0 = \{\emptyset, A^*\}$.
- Level $n + \tfrac{1}{2}$: the class of all finite unions of marked products of languages in $\mathcal{V}_n$.
- Level $n + 1$: the class of all Boolean combinations of languages that are marked products of languages in $\mathcal{V}_n$.

The union $\bigcup_{n} \mathcal{V}_n$ is exactly the class of star-free languages.

Problem. Find an algorithm that, given as input a half-integer $n \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{N}$ and a star-free language $L \subseteq A^*$ (presented, for instance, by a finite automaton or a finite syntactic monoid recognizing it), decides whether $L \in \mathcal{V}_n$. Equivalently, prove or disprove that membership in $\mathcal{V}_n$ is uniformly decidable across all levels $n$ of the hierarchy.
artifact.status_search_result: The membership problem for the Straubing-Thérien hierarchy is known to be decidable for levels 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, and, following work of Place and Zeitoun on separation and covering, for level 2 as well (and the corresponding half-integer level 5/2 is decidable in restricted settings such as two-letter alphabets, by Glaßer–Schmitz). However, decidability of membership at every level of the hierarchy remains open in general; the problem is solved only for finitely many low levels.

status_evidence.title: The Complexity of Separation for Levels in Concatenation Hierarchies
status_evidence.snippet: Separation is decidable for the levels 1/2, 1, 3/2 and 2 for both the dot-depth and Straubing-Thérien hierarchies.
status_evidence.claim: Membership and separation are known to be decidable up to level 2 of the Straubing-Thérien hierarchy.

status_evidence.title: New decidable upper bound of the second level in the Straubing-Thérien concatenation hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Decidable upper bound for level 2 in the Straubing-Thérien hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability results have been obtained for the second level of the hierarchy.

status_evidence.title: Level 5/2 of the Straubing-Thérien Hierarchy for Two-Letter Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Effective characterization of level 5/2 for two-letter alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Level 5/2 is decidable only in restricted alphabet settings; general decidability beyond level 2 is not established.
